promptLatex: In right triangle $ABC$ the right angle is at $C$. The altitude from $C$ meets hypotenuse $\overline{AB}$ at $D$, where $AD = 4$ and $DB = 9$. What is $AC + BC$?
hintLatex: Each leg of the big triangle is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse and its own segment.
Work out the hypotenuse first, then simplify each leg carefully.
solutionLatex:
The hypotenuse is $AB = AD + DB = 4 + 9 = 13$.

The altitude to the hypotenuse makes $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle CBD$ similar to the whole triangle, so each leg is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse and the segment it sits above.

That gives $AC = \sqrt{AD \cdot AB} = \sqrt{52} = 2\sqrt{13}$ and $BC = \sqrt{DB \cdot AB} = \sqrt{117} = 3\sqrt{13}$.

Adding them, $AC + BC = 5\sqrt{13}$.
